proposals.before: Within his jurisdiction he held sole authority over offenses up to and including capital crimes.
proposals.after: Within his jurisdiction he held sole authority over offenses short of capital crimes.
proposals.reason: 死罪以下 means offenses below capital crimes, not including capital punishment; the literal overstates his authority.

proposals.before: On wuzi day in the ninth month he executed xiangwen Balu, Zhuahen Du, and two others.
proposals.after: On wuzi day in the ninth month he executed xiangwen Balu, yila Hendun, and two others.
proposals.reason: 拽剌 is a Khitan office title (yila); 痕篤 is the personal name. Fusing them as Zhuahen Du obscures the office and name.

proposals.before: That night attendants Xiaoge, washer Huage, cook Xingu, and six others in all rebelled; the Emperor met assassination at age thirty-nine; his temple name was Muzong.
proposals.after: That night attendants Xiaoge, washer Huage, cook Xingu, and three others — six men in all — rebelled; the Emperor met assassination at age thirty-nine; his temple name was Muzong.
proposals.reason: 等六人 means six persons in total including the three named, not six additional persons.

decisions.reason: 死罪以下 means offenses below the capital grade, so sole jurisdiction stops short of capital crimes; the original 'up to and including capital crimes' overstates the authority.
詳穩八剌、拽剌痕篤 pairs office title with personal name in each case; 拽剌 is the yila office and 痕篤 the name, so Zhuahen Du wrongly fuses them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 殺詳穩八剌、拽剌痕篤等四人

decisions.reason: 等六人 counts six rebels in all, including the three named attendants; 'six others in all' wrongly adds six more people.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 近侍小哥、盥人花哥、庖人辛古等六人反

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0002 shows Zhuahen Du was invented by fusing the yila office title 拽剌 with the personal name 痕篤; s0111 supports no such alternate name.

claimRevisions.reason: Parallel to 詳穩/xiangwen for Balu, the title claim should be only 拽剌/yila; 痕篤 is the personal name already claimed in c0232.
